thread:
maria.g: IncidentBot alerted: S2 - sudden RPM spike on hosted Llama2-70b and Mistral-8x families. Seeing sustained 2.5x baseline for last 6m. paging aj and devin :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-042 - elevated per-model request rate. Suggested mitigations: apply per-model RPM/TMP caps, disable streaming for >32k tokens, enable burst queue.
pagerbot: @on-call shift started: aj on-call (us-west). Handoff ETA 02:00 UTC.
aj: I see the spike. Root requests are mostly from a single heavy customer and a few small bursts from bots. Samples look like long-context generation, lots of streaming sessions.
devin: can we confirm whether this is a client-side retry storm or actual traffic? engineered patterns show steady token churn, not retries.
maria.g: metrics: stream sessions up 3x, avg seq len +1.8x. latency and errors are creeping but still under SLO. Need live mitigation to protect multi-tenant nodes.
aj: Proposed fast mitigations (implement in this order):
1) Apply per-model RPM cap for hosted tier:

```json
{
  "action": "update_rate_limit",
  "scope": "model_family",
  "model_families": ["llama2-70b","mistral-8x"],
  "hosted_tier": {"rpm": 120, "tpm": 1800},
  "grace_period": 60
}
```

2) Disable server-side streaming for these families for hosted (fallback to non-streamed responses).
3) Add strict burst throttling rule for single-tenant IPs > 500 req/min.
aj: I can apply (1) and (3) now via admin console. Devin, can you flip off streaming?
devin: On it. Patching streaming flag now: `stream.enabled=false` for family filters. Applying canary to us-west-2 first.

[2m later]
devin: Canary flip succeeded on us-west-2, observed immediate drop in concurrent SSE connections for Llama2-70b. No errors so far.
aj: Rate limit change pushed to global guardrail. Config snippet applied to edge: `edge-ratelimit://v2/models?family=llama2-70b,mistral-8x&rpm=120&tpm=1800`
maria.g: Early telemetry: incoming RPM for Llama2-70b dropped from 320 -> 110 within 90s. Mistral-8x dropped from 250 -> 95. Latency improved.
nick.p: Noticed one enterprise customer (acme-corp) is hitting the cap and will see throttles. Their SLA is dedicated but they are on hosted trial — tag sent to account team. @maria.g please confirm customer impact.
maria.g: Contacted account team; they confirm Acme is in integration test, not production traffic. Logged customer-facing note and post to #support with mitigation details.
aj: Logging mitigation steps in the runbook and creating a short-lived policy so we can rollback. Also enabling alert escalation if 50% of requests are 429 post-mitigation.

[5m later]
incident-bot: Auto-scan shows a side-effect: small uptick in queueing for Dedicated pool when routing fallback triggers. Adding transient capacity allowed per policy.
devin: I increased dedicated burst nodes by 2 (hot standby) to reduce impact. Rolling back streaming flag for dedicated-only nodes so enterprise customers keep stream UX.

maria.g: Summary for ops: applied hosted-only caps for llama2-70b & mistral-8x rpm=120 tpm=1800, disabled hosted streaming for those families, added burst IP throttle. Dedicated unaffected except for extra capacity added. Impacted parties: Acme trial (not prod), internal integration tests.
aj: Next steps: keep caps for 1 hour, monitor 429 rates and latency. If stable, gradually relax tpm by 20% every 30m.

[20m after initial action]
maria.g: Telemetry stable. 429s at 2% of requests (acceptable) and CPU on inference nodes normalized. Reopening continuous monitoring dashboard.

aj: Preparing handoff to erin (next on-call). Leaving explicit runbook note and rollback commands.

```bash
# rollback snippet
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/rate-limits -d '{"action":"remove","scope":"model_family","model_families":["llama2-70b","mistral-8x"]}'
# re-enable streaming for hosted
curl -X PATCH https://admin.redwood.internal/feature-flags -d '{"stream.enabled":true, "filter":"family in (llama2-70b,mistral-8x)"}'
```

erin: taking over. Thanks @aj. I'll watch for the next 2hrs and will escalate to infra if 429 >5% or latency regresses. Any context I should know?
maria.g: note: one small svc (internal loadtester) caused ~30% of the spike; loadtester team alerted and paused. Also added temporary dashboard annotation.
erin: good. I'll keep the hosted caps in place and only relax after three clean 30m windows. If it looks good at 90m, I'll start ramp down. Handoff logged. :white_check_mark:
aj: thanks team. Closing incident thread when we hit stable-90m mark.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-042 status -> mitigated (actions applied). Ticket updated with notes and runbook links.
